# New sensing capability versus trustworthy measurement {#sec-session-05}

**Meeting 5 | Tuesday, October 6, 2026 | 1:00-2:00 PM Pacific**

## Central question

When does a new sensor change what can be discovered, and what must be established before its numbers count as physical evidence?

## The paper pair

**Pairing type:** Discovery-enabling instrument / calibration.

### Paper A: Illuminating seafloor faults and ocean dynamics with dark fiber distributed acoustic sensing

@lindsey2019. **Science (2019).** [Paper / publisher record](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aay5881)

Read the main subsea DAS article.

*Access: Publisher/DOI page; full text may require institutional access.*

### Paper B: On the Broadband Instrument Response of Fiber-Optic DAS Arrays

@lindsey2020. **Journal of Geophysical Research: Solid Earth (2020).** [Paper / publisher record](https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1029/2019JB018145) | [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1029/2019JB018145)

Read the instrument-response study’s calibration approach and discussion; a discussant inspects the response comparisons.

*Access: Publisher full-text page.*

### Why these papers belong together

The first study demonstrates an observational use of subsea telecom fiber. The second investigates a DAS array’s broadband response. A capability demonstration and a calibration study answer different questions; neither supplies a universal response for every installation. [@lindsey2019; @lindsey2020]

## Prepare before the meeting

Trace one familiar plotted quantity from physical process to instrument, digitization, calibration, processing, and interpretation.

## Discussion questions

1. What is measured along a fiber, and what is inferred about ground motion?
2. Could coupling, gauge length, or processing produce a spatial anomaly?
3. When is improved measurement itself a scientific advance?

## One-hour meeting

| Time | Activity |
|:--|:--|
| 0-10 min | Independent first judgments; surface disagreements. |
| 10-25 min | Compare the papers: claim, evidence, assumptions, and limits. |
| 25-45 min | Work through the case exercise below. |
| 45-55 min | Translate the discussion into agent requirements and tests. |
| 55-60 min | Record an output and one unresolved disagreement. |

### Case exercise

Compare two apparent amplitude anomalies: one caused by a physical change and one by a measurement-chain change. Specify what additional metadata or independent sensor would discriminate them. Do not require the group to implement a DAS simulator during the hour.

## Agent-design or evaluation output

Measurement-provenance checklist: observable, units, response, sampling, installation, transforms, uncertainty, and independent checks.

## Record after the meeting

Record the evidence for your main claim, what changed your mind, what remains unresolved, and one change to the agent or its evaluation. Keep confidential examples in private group notes rather than committing them to this public book.
